Tidy Queues, Tidy Mind

A queue is a promise to your future self, and like most promises it gets harder to keep the longer it sits. The oldest item in a reading list is usually the one you feel worst about and are least likely to read.

The fix that worked for me was embarrassingly simple. Once a week I go through the list from the top and make a decision about each item: read it now, keep it for later, or admit that I am never going to and delete it.

Deleting is the part people resist. It feels like losing something, but an unread link is not knowledge, it is an obligation. The café where I do this has learned to expect me on Thursdays.

What survives the weekly pass is a short list of things I actually want to read, which turns out to be the only kind of list that gets read.
